content:
Apple detailed the numerous security patches included in today's new operating system versions following the release of iOS 26.6, iPadOS 26.6 and related software updates.

The security updates in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 have multiple implications for iPhone and iPad

In iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, Apple detailed more than 75 security patches for iPhone and iPad, covering multiple areas of the system.

More precisely, Apple's bulletin contains 78 individual vulnerability entries, involving 87 independent CVE numbers. The number of CVEs is higher because some entries involve more than one CVE.

Apple did not indicate that any of the vulnerabilities patched in iOS 26.6 had been actively exploited in the wild.

Among Apple's lengthy list, several patches stand out:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote could allow an application to obtain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder could allow an application to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc could allow malicious applications to escape their sandbox.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation could allow malicious applications to bypass code signing enforcement.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted malicious files.
  • An issue in Accessibility could disclose sensitive information to a person with physical access through the iPhone Mirroring feature.
  • A vulnerability in Contacts could allow an application to add contacts without user authorisation.

Kernel, WebKit and Wi-Fi patches

Apple also patched more than ten kernel vulnerabilities. Potential impacts include corrupting or writing to kernel memory, disclosing kernel memory, bypassing network filters, and causing unexpected system termination.

WebKit also received a large number of patches. These vulnerabilities could lead to process memory disclosure, reveal whether a user has visited a particular link, cause interface spoofing, violate iframe sandboxing rules, allow an application to read files outside its sandbox, or cause Safari to crash.

In addition, a Wi-Fi vulnerability could allow a nearby attacker to corrupt process memory.

After the 78 documented security patches, Apple included an "Additional Recognition" section listing 12 acknowledgements.

These entries credit security researchers who assisted in the research, but are not treated as independent security patches and have not been assigned additional CVE numbers.

The full list of patches and researcher acknowledgements are available on Apple's website.

Security patches for Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro

Apple's newly published macOS Tahoe 26.6 security notes list a total of 155 independent CVEs.

In addition to many of the same patches as for iPhone and iPad, the Mac update also addresses vulnerabilities that could allow an application to obtain root privileges, escape the sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, and access protected data.

Apple also released security updates for older versions of macOS today, which are not included in the statistics of this article.

Apple also published patch details for watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6 and visionOS 26.6. After deduplicating overlaps between platforms, Apple's latest updates address a combined total of 194 independent CVEs.

Apple previously disclosed that, in response to AI-driven attack tools, several security patches were accelerated ahead of schedule in last month's iOS 26.5.2 release.
